subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nancy Rivers <nancy@peakhealth.com>
Cc: Jason Liu <jason@peakhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals / next steps

Hi Nancy / Jason —

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciate the candid overview of Peak Health's integration challenges. Wanted to capture the key pain points, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Quick recap below; I’ve attached a short telemetry spec and our evals catalog for reference.

Pain points you shared:
- Lack of end-to-end observability for LLM calls: no per-prompt tracing into downstream services, so it’s hard to diagnose latency and failure modes.
- Regression detection is manual: model updates and prompt changes have led to user-impacting regressions that weren’t caught by current alerts.
- No standard “golden prompt” sets and limited A/B rollout guardrails for staged model changes.
- Cost spikes during peak hours with unknown batching patterns.

Current stack (from the call):
- App/back-end: Kubernetes on GCP (GKE)
- Monitoring: Datadog for infra + application, Sentry for errors
- ML infra: a mix of hosted API for few features and internal self-hosted endpoints for others; evals are ad-hoc spreadsheets and CI checks.

Success criteria (what Peak Health needs to call this successful):
1) Per-route dashboards showing latency distribution, token-costs, and error rates (by model and route).
2) Tracing hooks from request -> model -> downstream services (to root-cause slow calls).
3) Golden prompt sets and automated regression alerts linked to PROMPT/semantic drift (daily smoke tests).
4) Rollout guardrails: canary policies, automatic rollback on quality regressions, and simple policy config for rollback thresholds.
5) A plan for a 30-day eval run with clear pass/fail criteria.

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood will: share the MVP telemetry spec (attached) and an evals catalog (attached).
- Schedule a 1-hour technical implementation session next week with your infra and security folks to review tracing hooks and entropy controls.
- Provision a 30-day eval environment (sandbox credentials & sample pipelines) and a suggested test plan for the golden prompts.
- Follow up with a rough MLP SOW and initial pricing for Dedicated/reserved capacity if you want predictable throughput.

As requested, I’ve attached: 1) 2026-03-22_peakhealth_mvp_telemetry_spec.pdf (telemetry fields, example dashboards) and 2) evals-catalog.xlsx (suggested golden prompts, smoke tests, regression alert examples).

Would next Wed (3/25) at 10am PT or Thu (3/26) at 11am PT work for the technical session?

Thanks,
Marissa

Nice to meet you both (virtually) — quick note from my side ahead of Wed:

I reviewed the evals-catalog.xlsx you sent over. For the golden prompt sets we recommend:
- 10–15 representative prompts per route (edge cases + high-frequency)
- A mix of deterministic and stochastic examples to validate both correctness and hallucination/regression metrics
- Baseline metrics: semantic similarity (BERTScore), factuality checks (fact-check snippets), and user-utility proxy (task completion rate)

For regression alerts we’ll propose two tiers:
- Safety/critical regressions: auto-rollback (e.g., major hallucination spike, latency > 2s p95)
- Quality regressions: notify + canary hold (e.g., drop below baseline BERTScore by X%)

I’ll bring a sample alert config and a suggested dashboard layout to the session.

See you Wed.

—Steph
